summary: Iteration 6 validated the new email/password JWT auth + change-password feature end-to-end on top of the existing Emergent Google OAuth. Backend: added TestEmailPasswordAuthAndChange (9 new tests) covering login success (JWT returned + httpOnly access_token cookie set), 401 on wrong password / unknown email, JWT Bearer accepted on /api/auth/me and /api/clients, legacy Google session_token=test_session_verify still accepted, change-password wrong-current -> 400, new_password < 6 chars -> 400, and full 'change -> old login fails -> new login works -> revert' round trip. Full suite now 55 passed / 1 skipped (Resend rate-limit) in 72s. Frontend (playwright, 1920x1080): /login shows login-email, login-password, login-submit-btn, change-password-link AND google-login-btn; wrong-password login shows readable 'Invalid email or password' in login-error; owner login lands on Dashboard and JWT (3-segment) is stored in localStorage.session_token; user menu exposes change-password-menu-btn which navigates to /change-password; on the change-password page, mismatched new/confirm shows cp-error 'New passwords do not match.'; a successful password change renders the change-password-success card; the password was reverted to RevivalPro2026! via the API in the same run (200) and a final owner login succeeds. Google button on /login still redirects to https://auth.emergentagent.com/oauth/... . Regression: /clients and /contracts still load when authenticated. Owner credentials are back to RevivalPro2026! at end of run.
action_items: OPTIONAL: /api/auth/change-password does not enforce rate-limiting or brute-force lockout on the current_password check (the auth_testing.md playbook mentions 5-attempt lockout). Currently unlimited attempts against a known email are possible.

OPTIONAL: /api/auth/change-password does not require the caller to be authenticated (email is in the body). This is deliberate so the /change-password link on /login works without a session, but consider requiring auth OR adding rate-limiting + captcha to prevent online password-guessing.

OPTIONAL: on the frontend, after a successful password change, the user is not automatically logged in with the new password nor redirected to /login - only the success card is shown. Consider auto-redirect to /login (with a small delay) so the flow completes.
OPTIONAL: JWT_SECRET / ADMIN_PASSWORD are read via os.environ - good - but the process would 500 (KeyError) if JWT_SECRET is ever unset. A clearer startup check would improve DX.
OPTIONAL: server.py is now ~1280 lines - splitting auth.py / contracts.py / public_sign.py / settings.py routers is overdue (unchanged from iter-5).
critical_code_review_comments: get_current_user tries the session_token (Google) path first and JWT path second, but both consult the same `bearer` variable. If a caller sends a JWT as Bearer and there happens to be a user_sessions row with that exact string (extremely unlikely for a JWT), the session-token branch would win. Not a practical bug but worth an explicit type discriminator (e.g. Bearer format check: JWTs have two dots).

POST /api/auth/login sets the access_token cookie with samesite='none' and secure=True which is correct for cross-site preview flows, but there is no Path scoping or Domain and no HttpOnly refresh-token pair; a single 7-day access token is the whole session. Consider a shorter access token + refresh flow.

POST /api/auth/change-password does not invalidate existing sessions/JWTs after a successful password change - a stolen JWT remains valid for its 7-day life. Consider bumping a `password_changed_at` on the user and rejecting JWTs with iat < password_changed_at.

seed_admin() updates the admin's password_hash on every startup if it detects a mismatch - great for recovery, but combined with hot-reload it means anyone with .env write access can silently rotate the admin creds on next restart. Log this action.
Frontend stores the JWT in localStorage (XSS-exposed). The httpOnly cookie is also set, so the LS copy is redundant and adds XSS risk; consider dropping it and relying on the cookie.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The auth suite adds 9 new tests (55 total). IMPORTANT: TestEmailPasswordAuthAndChange must remain a SINGLE class - pytest-xdist loadscope pins all methods of one class to one worker, so change-password mutations do not race against concurrent logins on another worker. If you split it back into two classes you will see intermittent 401s on jwt_bearer_* tests during the temp-change window. When testing the /change-password UI flow ALWAYS revert via `POST /api/auth/change-password {email: tccrossmusic@gmail.com, current_password: <temp>, new_password: RevivalPro2026!}` in a finally/emergency block or you will lock out the shared owner account. Frontend stores JWT in localStorage.session_token (3-segment JWT). Google button on /login navigates to https://auth.emergentagent.com/oauth/?redirect=<origin>/ - still working. /login redirects to / when already authenticated, so clear localStorage before re-testing the login page.
